home.title: Laura Rentería — Brand Strategy, Creative Direction & Image Consulting
home.description: Consultant in branding, creative direction and personal brand. I build brands and the people who represent them. New York · Colombia.

hero.headline: I build brands. And the people who represent them.
hero.subhead: Brand strategy, creative direction and image consulting for companies, founders and professionals who intend to be remembered.

manifesto.statement: Everything communicates. Silence communicates. The wait communicates. So does what you chose not to show.

lines.a: Nobody buys what they don't understand.
lines.b: Being good isn't enough. You have to be legible.

about.headline: I'm Laura Rentería.
about.lead: I work where three things meet: strategy, aesthetics and the person.
about.body1: My background combines communications, marketing and advertising, image consulting and fashion PR. My work has been digital strategy, creative direction, content production, branding and brand experience across industries that have very little in common with one another.
about.body2: In 2018 I founded Renace Fashion Studio. For years I worked with models, founders and professionals on how they looked, how they spoke and how they showed up. That's where I understood the thing that defines how I work now:
about.pull: A brand can have flawless strategy and still fail, because the person representing it can't carry it.
about.close: So I do both. I build the brand. And I develop the person behind it.

services.headline: How I can help
services.subhead: You can work on one or all three. Most projects start with one and end up touching the other two.

process.headline: A method, not a formula
process.subhead: The order never changes. The content always does.
process.footnote: Every project begins with a diagnostic conversation. I don't take work without one, because I wouldn't know what I was solving.

steps.title: Listen
steps.body: We start with a long conversation. Not a form: an actual conversation where I understand the business, the moment, what's working, what's uncomfortable, and the thing you haven't been able to name for a while.
steps.deliverable: A diagnostic session and a written record of what I found.

steps.title: Diagnose
steps.body: I review what exists — the brand, the competitors, the content, current perception, and the presence of whoever represents it. This is usually where the incoherences nobody wanted to look at directly come to the surface.
steps.deliverable: Brand and presence audit, with clear priorities.

steps.title: Define
steps.body: The hard decisions get made. Positioning, territory, audience, tone, visual direction. Fewer options, more judgement.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: Execution. Identity, content, campaigns, scripts, experiences, wardrobe, presence training — whatever the project needs, in the order that makes sense.

steps.title: Stay
steps.body: The brand meets the world, and that's where it gets interesting. We adjust, measure, correct. Nothing is born finished.

work.headline: The work, in detail
work.subhead: Projects where the brand and the person were built at the same time.
work.placeholder: Case studies are published with each client's permission. Some projects are covered by confidentiality and don't appear here. If you'd like to see work relevant to your sector, write to me and I'll share it privately.

items.a: Companies that need brand clarity, founders who've become the face of their business, and professionals building a position of their own. I've worked in fashion, beauty, hospitality, nightlife and professional services. Sector matters less than moment: this works best when there's something real to put in order.

items.q: Do you only work with large brands?
items.a: No. I work with projects that are just starting and with brands that have existed for years. What I do need is a willingness to make decisions. Projects that stall almost never stall over budget — they stall over indecision.

items.q: How long does a project take?
items.a: A 1:1 consultation resolves in a single session. A branding project usually runs six to ten weeks. Personal brand and presence work is better in three-month cycles.

items.q: Do you work in person or remotely?
items.a: Both. I work between New York and Colombia, and I run projects remotely without difficulty. For production, on-set direction and presence training, being in the room changes the result significantly.

items.q: What if I'm not sure what I need?
items.a: That's the most common situation there is. That's what the diagnostic conversation is for — you leave it knowing what you need, whether or not you work with me.

closing.statement: Let's talk about what you're building.
closing.body: Tell me where you are. If I can help, I'll say so. If I can't, I'll say that too — and tell you who can.
closing.microcopy: I take a limited number of projects each quarter.

cta.statement: Not sure which one you need?
cta.body: That's normal. Write to me and we'll work it out in the first conversation.

creative-direction.tagline: Deciding who you are before deciding how you look.
creative-direction.overview: Positioning, identity, brand architecture, creative direction, and everything that makes a brand recognisable without a signature.
who: Brands being born, brands that grew without direction, and brands that no longer resemble what they claim to be.
New ventures, and existing brands that need an identity matching what they've already become.
Brands that need a campaign, a launch, a visual reset — or simply content that looks like what they charge for.

digital-marketing.tagline: Turning strategy into something people see, understand and remember.
digital-marketing.overview: Content with judgement, not content by volume. Deciding where to be, how often, and with what message, based on what the business actually needs this year.
who: Businesses spending on marketing without clarity on what's working.
Brands and professionals whose profile doesn't match the quality of their work.
Teams and founders producing a great deal and connecting very little.

image-consulting.tagline: How you look, how you speak, how you appear, and what stays after you leave the room.
image-consulting.overviewSubhead: It's about the impression you leave matching what you're actually capable of.
image-consulting.overview: Most image consulting ends in the wardrobe. This one starts there. Because clothing is only the first layer. After it comes how you enter a room. How you stand when someone speaks to you. What you do with your hands in front of a camera. How you tell your story in thirty seconds without sounding like a résumé. All of that can be worked on. And all of it decides whether you're taken seriously.
who: Founders who became the face of their business.
Professionals who need visibility to grow.
People about to appear in media, on stage or on camera.
Talent and models building a career.
